articles.title: Volkanovski Responds to Age Talk, Calls for Gaethje Retirement Super Fight | UFC 333
articles.description: Alex Volkanovski is in Abu Dhabi ahead of his featherweight title defense against undefeated Movsar Evloev at UFC 333. At media day, Volk answered the question everyone is asking: has he gotten old at 38? He says the headlines after Saturday will read "one of Volk's best performances yet." Volkanovski also explained his idea of a champion-vs-champion retirement super fight with Justin Gaethje, said he'd beat Evloev even in a pure grappling match, talked about tying Jose Aldo's featherweight title-defense record, Cooking with Volk, his Alexander Volkov mix-ups, and who's coming to Abu Dhabi to watch him fight. ⏱️ CHAPTERS 0:00 Emotions ahead of the Movsar Evloev title defense 0:36 "Has Volk gotten old?" — answering the age narrative 1:53 Athleticism vs. fight IQ at 38 3:18 Justin Gaethje super fight and a retirement fight 5:34 Bouncing back after the Islam and Topuria losses 7:19 Finishing fast: an anniversary present for his wife 8:22 Top-three all-time? articles.title: Alexander Volkanovski Just Called Out Justin Gaethje#ufc
articles.description: Alexander Volkanovski calling out Justin Gaethje? Chael Sonnen absolutely loves it. Chael explains why this is a callout that deserves respect. Arman Tsarukyan has made it clear he believes he's the No. 1 contender, while Ilia Topuria remains part of the lightweight title conversation. Meanwhile, Gaethje has indicated he isn't looking to fight until next year — and few fighters have directly called him out. Volkanovski could change that. He's willing to move up a weight class and face one of the toughest names in the division, while also giving Gaethje something he's been asking for: a new opponent. For Chael, that's what makes the challenge so impressive. Volkanovski isn't simply demanding a title shot. He's putting his name forward for a dangerous fight against an established contender. Would you watch Volkanovski vs. Gaethje? articles.title: Jon Jones Won't Solve Jake Paul's Francis Ngannou Problem
articles.description: Jake Paul wants Dana White to release Jon Jones so Jones can finally fight Francis Ngannou. Chael Sonnen understands why Jake wants the fight, but he believes Jake is trying to solve the wrong problem. Chael explains why Jon Jones vs. Francis Ngannou is no longer the biggest heavyweight fight in MMA, why Ngannou needs to help create an opponent people actually want to see him fight, and what happens if Jake signs Jones only to end up with two expensive heavyweight stars and nowhere to go next. articles.title: Jose Aldo Would Cut #1 Ranked Evloev
articles.description: Jose Aldo had some harsh words for Movsar Evloev, saying that despite being the No. 1 contender and capable of beating anyone, Evloev doesn't sell and puts on boring fights. Chael Sonnen doesn't like how Aldo said it, but he believes Aldo is right. Chael explains why winning alone isn't enough to become the face of a UFC division, what Alexander Volkanovski understands that Evloev still needs to learn, and why this week could be the biggest marketing opportunity of Evloev's career. If he becomes champion, Chael says Evloev needs more than a belt. He needs to give fans a reason to care about who he fights next. articles.title: Sean Strickland Has a Decision to Make
articles.description: Use my code CHAEL to get up to 50% off your Hume Pod: https://sponsr.is/humehealth_chael #HumeHealth #smartscale #weightloss Sean Strickland just signed a new UFC contract, and the UFC is saying publicly that there is no contract dispute. So why does the proposed Nassourdine Imavov rematch keep sliding, from December into the new year, with nothing about the fight itself changing? Chael Sonnen says there is only one real question here: does Sean still want to fight? Chael walks through the whole picture. The Imavov fight was Sean's idea in the first place: he refused to pass over the next contender the way he had been passed over himself. Something changed, and nobody can call him scared, because he has already done it. What fans do not see is the Sean Strickland of the practice room, the captain who coaches, holds teammates accountable, and lives by whatever he says out loud. That is the same trait that made him call out Israel Adesanya in Australia and then go do it, and it is the trait Chael worries about now: Sean gets locked in. He is not going to renegotiate a contract that was just renegotiated. If he wants more on top, he has to bring something different to the table, and his one red-hot argument is a Chimaev rematch. First base before home plate. So what does Sean do now? articles.title: Undefeated and Unemployed
articles.description: Use my code CHAEL to get up to 50% off your Hume Pod: https://sponsr.is/humehealth_chael #HumeHealth #smartscale #weightloss Farid Basharat is 16-0 as a professional and 7-0 inside the Octagon, and the UFC just let him walk. He fought out his contract, was never offered a new one, and became one of the biggest stories of the week, with Dana White telling reporters at UFC Edmonton that "there's definitely a reason." Chael Sonnen has studied this sport every single day of his life, has missed exactly one UFC card ever, and had never heard of Basharat until the release. And Chael says that is not his fault. It is somebody's fault. Historically, one thing kept a fighter safe no matter what: winning. You could be a complete jerk and winning protected you. Basharat and Muhammad Mokaev may be the only two fighters in history to fight out their contracts undefeated and not be re-signed, and it nearly happened to Colby Covington too. So where did it break down? Chael reads Basharat's statement and spots the tell in one word, "whom," a word no fighter writes, which means management wrote it, the same management that has other fighters to protect and a UFC relationship to maintain. Chael is not kicking a man while he is down. He is offering to help: meet him in Las Vegas this weekend, come to Real American Freestyle, and get in front of people. But if winning no longer protects you, the sport has a new culture, and everybody in it needs to hear that. articles.title: Bruce Buffer finds Josh Hokit disrespectful #ufc
articles.description: Josh Hokit has made his feelings known, but Chael Sonnen believes there's a harsh reality he needs to understand about the fight business. Chael breaks down Hokit's comments about his importance to the UFC and why he believes the attitude comes across as disrespectful. In MMA, a fighter's value can change quickly. A couple of bad results can mean a different paycheck, a lower spot on the card, and a much shorter path to the exit. Meanwhile, Chael points out that Bruce Buffer's future earning power looks very different from a fighter's. It's a reminder that being part of the UFC doesn't guarantee long-term security. Hokit has pushed back against the criticism, bringing up the bad guys and criminals who have been part of the fight game. But will that response help his case? Chael explains why the business of fighting can be unforgiving — and why a fighter's next performance can matter more than he realizes. articles.title: Charles Won't Change His Style for the BMF
articles.description: Use my code CHAEL to get up to 50% off your Hume Pod: https://sponsr.is/humehealth_chael #HumeHealth #smartscale #weightloss Charles Oliveira beat Max Holloway for the BMF belt, and a loud part of the fanbase decided he fought the wrong way: too much of the fight on the ground, not enough standing in the middle and slugging. The call was actually made that he should give the belt back. Oliveira's answer was simple: he is not changing his style because he is fighting for the BMF belt, and Chael Sonnen says he is right. Chael traces the style argument back to where it started, 1993, when the UFC was formed and nobody actually knew whether wrestling, boxing, or grappling was the best way to win a fight. It got settled then, and it has been settled ever since: you bring every tool you have, and the whole thing has always been about who can beat up the other guy. But that leaves the real question. If the BMF is not about record, and it is not about style, what is it? Chael's answer: veteran status, and you will know it when you see it. Cub Swanson is a BMF. The Diaz brothers and Jorge Masvidal obviously are. Diego Lopes changes what the word means. And if the matchmakers want a guaranteed slugfest, that is a booking problem, not a fighter problem. Book Mike Perry. He will give you one. articles.title: What Really Drives Alexander Volkanovski
articles.description: The story of Alexander Volkanovski is not being told accurately, and Chael Sonnen is going to fix that. Volk is the one champion with real leverage behind the scenes who has never once used it. He has never tried to renegotiate, never tried to get out of a fight, and where every other champion angles for the biggest paycheck against the easiest opponent, Volkanovski goes out of his way to fight the hardest guy available. Movsar Evloev is 19-0 and has beaten former world champions, and Volk asked for him anyway. Now Volk says he will stop Evloev, then he wants Justin Gaethje. Chael says the Gaethje fight is not coming, and explains why that does not matter: people have been calling Volkanovski's next fight his last one for three years, Daniel Cormier was once prepared to give him a retirement send-off on commentary, and the thing still driving Volk is the one thing he has never done. Along the way, Chael makes the point every fighter needs to hear: nobody remembers your record, not even the fighters themselves. The most valuable thing a win gives you is not the belt. It is a platform, and Volk is positioned to use his. Then I'm going to fight Justin Gaethje." 3:08 Why the Gaethje fight isn't coming 3:46 Three years of "this is Volk's last fight" 4:34 The one thing he's never done is still driving him 5:37 Nobody remembers your record. articles.title: Dricus Du Plessis Is Getting in His Own Way
articles.description: Nobody has ever played the promotion game better than Dricus Du Plessis, and Chael Sonnen can prove it. Dricus was an interchangeable undercard fighter until he did the one thing nobody else would do: he complained. When Bo Nickal got better card placement than him, Dricus spoke up, and when a slot opened, the UFC went straight to the only guy who asked for it. He beat Darren Till, talked his way into a co-main event, and knocked off Robert Whittaker as a 2.5-to-1 underdog. That parlayed into a world title and one of the hottest feuds the sport has ever seen. But since the Khamzat Chimaev loss, Dricus has gone quiet, and Chael says that is the one mistake a guy like him cannot make. Now Dricus says he cuts 45 pounds to make middleweight, wants his belt back at 185, and then wants the light heavyweight title too. Chael explains why that exact path did not work the way people remember for Alex Pereira, why the Chimaev matchup is simply a bad one for him, and why if Dricus wants 205, the time is right now, not after another run at a belt he plans to leave behind. Chapters: 0:00 The squeaky wheel: how Dricus talked his way off the undercard 2:00 He beat Whittaker, and the hottest feud in the sport was born 3:33 The Chimaev loss, and why going quiet is the one mistake he can't make 4:13 A main event with Kamaru Usman, off a loss 5:19 The Strickland argument: "I beat the champion twice" 6:20 Cutting 45 pounds, and the 185-then-205 plan 6:46 The Pereira story everybody tells wrong 8:02 If you want 205, go now 8:17 Some matchups are just bad matchups #ChaelSonnen #DricusDuPlessis #UFC #MMA #Middleweight

articles.title: Does the UFC Secretly Love Josh Hokit?
articles.description: Ask Uncle Chael is back, and this week's questions hit everything: marriage, folkstyle, a fight Chael says was stopped on a tap that never happened, and whether the UFC hates Josh Hokit. Jeff Finnegan leads off: should I have kids? Then CJS sets a wrestling round robin between Spencer Lee, Ono, and Roman Bravo-Young, and somebody has to go 0-2. Anthony asks whether to lock in on fitness and his own business first or find a wife at the same time, and Chael flips the order entirely: the wife is the one you want the most, and you do all of it at once. BOD asks why folkstyle is not popular on the world scene, and Chael explains why the American style no other country wrestles may be exactly why Americans run MMA. A fan asks about a fourth fight with Jeremy Horn, Eric Sands asks whether a man proving everyone wrong is living on his enemies' terms, and Chael tells the Florida story: Trevor Prangley, a submission stoppage he says he never tapped to, and a brutal locker-room interrogation by the commission. Plus why every great story needs a villain, why David Robert Web's geography numbers are fake news, and the Hokit question: Ciryl Gane got the promo video, Hokit got no mention, so does the UFC hate him? Chael's answer is a list of everything the UFC has handed him. The final question is a fan's top five UFC fighters of all time, and Chael wants the gold, silver, and bronze medals for himself. articles.title: Is Ilia Topuria Thinking About Retirement? #ufc
articles.description: Could Ilia Topuria walk away from the UFC while he's still at the top? Chael Sonnen raises a surprising possibility: with money in the bank and an already remarkable career, could Ilia decide he's accomplished enough and retire earlier than anyone expects? Chael also looks at the championship implications. If Ilia steps aside, what happens to the title picture? Would a potential fight with Arman Tsarukyan need to be for the championship, and where does Paddy Pimblett fit into the equation? Rather than assume he knows what Ilia wants, Chael says he plans to reach out to Ilia's manager to get answers directly. Is retirement a realistic possibility, or does Ilia still have unfinished business in the UFC? articles.title: Bruce Buffer Crossed a Line With Josh Hokit
articles.description: Bruce Buffer weighed in on Josh Hokit, and Chael Sonnen says it breaks the one rule production people are never supposed to break. To explain it, he tells the Arianny Celeste story, and the phone call that taught him how this business actually works. After the first Anderson Silva fight, Chael was told Arianny had said she was glad it happened to him, for all the trash he talked. He fired back. Then came the call: why did you go after her? She is off limits. There is a separation. Fighters on one side, production on the other, and the people paid to make fighters look good stay completely unbiased. The twist: Arianny never said it. She was innocent, and Chael clears her completely. The point stands anyway. Now Bruce. Chael puts it at a one out of ten, and thinks Buffer was actually trying to put Hokit over, then hedged with "I don't agree with everything he says" to keep his own hands clean, the same trap that ended Trent Lott. But look at the asymmetry. Hokit does not know when his next paycheck is, and two bad nights can end his career. Five years from now Bruce is still clearing seven figures, and if Bruce does not show up tonight, business does not change. If Josh does not, it does. And Hokit answered: this game licenses criminals and men fresh out of prison, while he has a degree, All-American honors, a family, and a spotless record, and he is outworking Ciryl Gane at the media game. Why is the announcer the one bringing him down? The closing: Chael softens it. Bruce really did not say anything that bad, it just was not nice and was not meant to elevate Hokit; it looked like Buffer wanted to disassociate himself. And if you want to be in the cage fighting business without getting your hands dirty, who exactly do you disassociate with? Chael remembers when people tried to disassociate from Joe Rogan: it disgusted him, he has not forgiven any of them, and he would not trust or do business with a single one, because they showed him who they are. His prediction: you will never hear about this again, it goes away. But Hokit is not a good guy to come after. If you come after him, you are going to take a bump, and when you do, you need to know you had it coming. 0:00 The Arianny story Chael has to tell first 0:51 The call: she's off limits, there's a separation 1:35 The twist, she never said it 2:25 Production makes fighters look good, and stays unbiased 3:04 Now we have Bruce Buffer and Josh Hokit 3:38 A one out of ten, but it still happened 4:23 Buffer tried to put him over, then covered himself 4:37 The Trent Lott lesson: association gets your hands dirty 6:30 Josh doesn't know when his next paycheck is 6:50 Bruce will clear seven figures either way 7:34 Hokit answers: criminals get licenses in this game 8:05 A degree, an All-American, and never in trouble 8:53 Bruce really didn't say anything that bad 9:09 If you don't want dirty hands, who do you disassociate with? 9:22 The Rogan lesson: Chael remembers who walked away 9:54 Prediction: you'll never hear about it again #UFC #MMA #JoshHokit

articles.title: Henry Cejudo Is Wrong About Alex Pereira #ufc
articles.description: Henry Cejudo says Alex Pereira needs to win two or three more fights before talking about another title shot. Chael Sonnen isn't buying it. At 40 years old and competing in a division where he has yet to win, Pereira faces a difficult road. But Chael makes a compelling argument: if Pereira is being offered a rematch against the very fighter who already beat him, how is that being spoiled with opportunities? Chael breaks down why Pereira's situation is more complicated than Cejudo makes it sound, and why Alex has earned more respect for the way he fought his way to the top. Is Alex Pereira getting special treatment from the UFC, or has he earned the right to pursue another opportunity?
